newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says India strike cargo backlogs clear.
newsitem.headline: KLM says India strike cargo backlogs clear.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said it has already managed to clear airfreight backlogs created by this weekend's air traffic control strike in India.
The strike began on April 11 and was called off at around 1130 GMT on Saturday.
Four KLM flights were diverted and three were cancelled altogether during the strike, said a KLM Cargo spokesman.
The three that were cancelled were Amsterdam- Bangkok-Taipei, Amsterdam-Singapore-Jakarta and Amsterdam-Kuala Lumpur-Manila.
"Cargo was re-booked on the first available flights," said the spokesman. He estimated that at most, cargo was delayed for 20 hours.
He added that cargo was not so difficult to deal with as passengers.
At Amsterdam Schiphol airport alone, the carrier had to accommodate 540 passengers in hotels and 300 passengers in Karachi and Dubai were also stranded and had to be accommodated, said the spokesman.
